questions.question: Nine harnesses have no rules directory at all. Should a `rule` fall back to the instruction block there, the way a command falls back to a skill?

options.label: Emulate only unscoped rules (Recommended)
options.description: A rule with no path scoping is already always-on, so folding it into the instruction block is semantically identical — emulate it. A rule that declares `paths:` is scoped on purpose; folding it in would make it always-on and spend context every session, which is a different behaviour wearing the same name. Refuse that one as unsupported.
options.preview:
rule with no `paths:`
  → emulated into the AGENTS.md block
     semantics unchanged ✓

rule with `paths: ["src/**"]`
  → unsupported on that harness
     "scoping this rule requires a rules
      directory; codex has none"

The distinction: command→skill preserved
semantics exactly. rule→instruction only
does when the rule was never scoped.

options.label: Always emulate
options.description: Any rule folds into the instruction block on a harness without a rules directory. Maximum coverage — every rule reaches every harness — at the cost of silently converting scoped guidance into always-on context, which is both a semantic change and a per-session token cost the user never asked for.

options.label: Never emulate — report unsupported
options.description: A rule installs only where a real rules directory exists. Most honest: harnaas never quietly changes what an asset does. But it means nine harnesses get no rules at all, including ones where the rule would have worked perfectly as always-on guidance.

questions.question: Someone edits inside the managed block in AGENTS.md. What does harnaas do?

options.label: Report as drift, don't clobber (Recommended)
options.description: Exactly the same rule as any other managed destination: lint reports it, install leaves it alone, and `--force` restores the generated content. Consistent with the model everywhere else, and it means an edit inside the block is never silently destroyed — which matters more here, since merge conflicts will land in this block.
options.preview:
$ harnaas lint
  error  AGENTS.md — managed block edited
         outside harnaas
         harnaas install --force restores it

$ harnaas install
  skipped  AGENTS.md block (locally modified)

$ harnaas install --force
  updated  AGENTS.md block

Same semantics as a drifted file.
Nothing new to learn.

options.label: Regenerate unconditionally
options.description: The block is entirely harnaas's, so every install rewrites it and edits inside it are meaningless by definition. Simplest possible rule and the block can never go stale — but it silently destroys whatever someone typed there, which contradicts the protection every other destination gets.

options.label: Report drift, and block the whole install
options.description: Treat an edited block as a hard error that fails the run rather than a skipped destination, on the grounds that AGENTS.md is load-bearing for every harness and a stale block is worse than a stale skill. Stronger signal, at the cost of one edited region stopping unrelated assets from installing.

questions.question: Five harnesses need personas in TOML, YAML, TypeScript, or a single shared document rather than markdown. How much of that does v1 specify?

options.label: Define the hook, implement two renderers (Recommended)
options.description: The adapter interface declares a per-type render step now, so no future adapter has to bend the design. v1 implements only the two it needs: identity (copy verbatim) and the command-to-skill emulator. Format conversion is specified as a capability, not written.

Future adapters become pure data — but it is a large amount of specification for formats nothing exercises, and the details will likely be wrong until a real adapter tests them.

options.description: harnaas installs markdown assets, and a harness that needs another format is permanently unsupported for that type. Sharply limits the tool's reach, but every write is a copy and the whole render/digest question disappears.

The frontier is empty. Every branch has been visited; nothing is silently assumed. Here's the shared understanding, consolidated.

## What harnaas is

A CLI for **team standardization**: a repo declares its harness assets, `harnaas install` materializes them, `harnaas lint` gates CI on them staying correct and current. Go, cobra, Charm v2, architecture imported from entire.io. Module `github.com/harnaas/harnaas`.

**Five asset types.** `skill` · `rule` · `instruction` · `command` · `persona`. `instruction` and `rule` split on a real distinction — instruction is committed and survives a fresh clone, rule is gitignored and can be glob-scoped.

**Manifest** (`harnaas.json`, hand-edited, root only): a `sources` block declaring repos and refs once, plus assets as plain strings. Type and id inferred from the path — `skills/review` is a skill called review. Strict decoding.

**Targets.** Shared-first: `.agents/skills/` reaches 17 harnesses, an AGENTS.md marker block reaches 21, and CLAUDE.md gets one `@AGENTS.md` line to bridge Claude Code. Per-harness adapters add only what's left — rules, commands, personas. v1 ships one named adapter and broad shared coverage. Removed surfaces are refused, gated ones are written with a note.

**Install** converges: removing an asset deletes its files, but only ones recorded in the lockfile whose content still matches. Unmanaged paths are never touched, on any flag. Two independent digests — source (did upstream move?) and installed (did someone edit it?) — which is what lets harnaas render as well as copy: a command becomes a skill with model-invocation disabled where no command surface exists, and an *unscoped* rule folds into the instruction block, while a scoped one is refused rather than silently made always-on.

**Lint** is read-only and always. Findings carry a runnable fix. Being behind a newer tag is an **error**, and so is tracking a branch — the only green state is pinned and current. `--frozen` checks the lockfile against the manifest with no files or network, which is the fast PR gate.

**Version control.** Installed files are gitignored via a managed block listing exact paths, so a hand-written skill sitting next to an installed one stays tracked.

## Where that leaves the specs

Roughly 60% of the 79 requirements I wrote are now wrong or incomplete. `harness-targets` is worst — its *Managed Rule Reference Block* requirement describes a mechanism we've since established doesn't exist, and its destination mapping predates the shared-target decision. `harnaas-manifest` needs the sources block, inference, and the fifth type. `lint-command` and `update-detection` need the severity inversion. `cli-foundation` and `init-command` survive largely intact.

Three of my own factual claims were wrong during this session and are corrected in the record: `.claude/rules/` exists (I said invent a workaround), AGENTS.md is *not* natively loaded by Claude Code (I said it was), and the skills cap is 1 MB not 64 KB.

# Ownership lives in the lockfile, not in a marker inside the file

harnaas needs to know which files under `.agents/` and `.claude/` it may update or delete and which
are the user's. The entire.io CLI, whose architecture harnaas otherwise copies, solves this by
embedding an `ENTIRE-MANAGED …` marker in every file it writes. harnaas records ownership in
`harnaas.lock.json` instead: a destination recorded there is managed, and a destination absent from it
is never overwritten or deleted, on any flag.

## Considered Options

The marker approach was rejected because entire.io *generates* the content it scaffolds and is
therefore free to add a line to it, whereas harnaas *copies* content verbatim from upstream. Injecting
a marker would mean the installed bytes never equal the source bytes — which would defeat the digest
comparison that `harnaas lint` uses to distinguish "you edited this" from "upstream changed this".
The mechanism meant to enable the check would have destroyed it. A marker would also be invalid
syntax in formats that carry no comment form.

## Consequences

Deleting the lockfile does not orphan installed files; it makes them unmanaged, which is protective
rather than destructive. A project with pre-existing harness files gets conflict reports on its first
install rather than a silent takeover. Both follow from the rule and are intended.

The exception is content harnaas authors itself rather than copies — the block in `AGENTS.md` and the
block in `.gitignore` — where a marker is correct precisely because there are no upstream bytes to
stay equal to. See [0003](./0003-instruction-content-in-an-agents-md-block.md).

# Skills install to the shared `.agents/` directory before a harness's own

A survey of 23 AI coding harnesses found that 17 of them read `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, and
21 read `AGENTS.md`. harnaas therefore writes skills to the shared location first and falls back to a
harness's own directory only where that harness does not read the shared one. The obvious design —
one directory tree per harness — is deliberately not what we do.

## Considered Options

Per-harness directories (`.claude/skills/`, `.cursor/skills/`, …) are more explicit: declaring a
harness would mean something concrete, and ownership would be unambiguous. They were rejected because
they produce N byte-identical copies of every skill, N lockfile installations, and N things to keep in
step — to buy explicitness the ecosystem has already stopped needing.

## Consequences

Two costs are accepted deliberately.

A shared directory is visible to **every** installed harness, not only the ones listed in
`harnaas.json`. The `harnesses` list therefore means "which harnesses we guarantee", not "which
harnesses will see this".

Ownership in the shared directory is a 17-way problem rather than a 2-way one, and other tools write
there too — `openspec` among them. The lockfile rule in
[0001](./0001-ownership-lives-in-the-lockfile.md) is what makes this safe: another tool's file at a
destination harnaas wants is simply an unmanaged conflict, reported and never overwritten.

# Instruction content goes in a marked block inside AGENTS.md

`instruction` assets are always-on guidance that must survive a fresh clone without anyone running
install, which means they have to live in a committed file the project already reads. harnaas writes
them into a marker-delimited block in `AGENTS.md` — read natively by 21 of 23 surveyed harnesses —
and adds a single `@AGENTS.md` line to `CLAUDE.md` to bridge Claude Code, which does not read
`AGENTS.md` at all.

## Considered Options

Two alternatives were examined and rejected.

**A file harnaas owns outright, pulled in by an import line.** Much the nicer model: ownership is
total, drift is a whole-file comparison, and no marker parsing is needed. Rejected because import
syntax exists in only about 6 of 23 harnesses — Codex, Cursor, Pi, Zed, Continue, Augment, Trae, Warp
and Factory have none — so every other harness would need a marker block regardless, and we would
build and maintain both mechanisms to use the nicer one a quarter of the time.

**Not writing into user-owned files at all**, which is `openspec init`'s central design rule. It
ships a legacy-cleanup module whose only job is un-writing marker blocks its own older versions added
to `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md`. That rule works for openspec because its single artifact can live in a
tool-owned subtree; harnaas's `instruction` type is *defined* as content in a file the user owns, so
there is no subtree to retreat into. We are knowingly re-adopting what openspec removed, for a
requirement openspec does not have.

## Consequences

Drift is region-level rather than file-level, and merge conflicts will land inside the block. Both are
accepted. Everything outside the markers is preserved byte-for-byte, an edit inside the block is
reported and never silently overwritten, and the block is removed entirely when the last instruction
asset goes away.

# An available update is a lint error, not a warning

`harnaas lint` exits non-zero when any asset is behind a newer tag, and also when any asset tracks a
mutable ref such as a branch. The only state that passes is one where every source is pinned to a tag
or commit and is current. Nearly every comparable tool treats an available update as advisory; this
one does not.

## Considered Options

Treating updates as warnings was the initial design, and it was rejected because harnaas exists to
make a team's harness configuration uniform and current — a warning that CI tolerates indefinitely
does not achieve that.

Branch-tracking assets are errors too, for a specific reason: a branch moves whenever upstream
commits, so if a moved branch were reported as "outdated" there would be no stable passing state at
all and CI would be permanently red. Reporting it instead as "not pinned, not reproducible" gives the
user an achievable fix — pin it — and makes the forcing function coherent rather than infinite.

## Consequences

`harnaas lint` is not deterministic across time: a project can pass today and fail tomorrow because
somebody upstream published a tag, with no local change. This is inherent to enforcing currency and is
mitigated by `--offline`, which performs every local check and skips the network entirely, for callers
who need a time-invariant result.

Exit code `2` is reserved for findings so that a red pipeline distinguishes "lint found problems" from
"lint itself failed" — the one place harnaas extends the exit-code contract it inherited from
entire.io.

# harnaas — settled design (40 decisions)

Authoritative. Where this contradicts an existing spec file, this wins.

## 0. Product

- **Audience: team standardization.** A repo declares its harness assets; everyone gets the same set;
  CI enforces it. Personal portability is secondary.
- Go CLI, module `github.com/harnaas/harnaas`, binary `cmd/harnaas`.
- Architecture and stack imported from the entire.io CLI at `github.com/entireio/cli`.
- Three commands: `init`, `install`, `lint`. No `add`/`remove`/`update`/`uninstall`.

## 1. Vocabulary (canonical — see CONTEXT.md at repo root)

- **Harness** — an AI coding tool that reads config from a project or user home. *Avoid: agent.*
- **Asset** — one unit of harness configuration. *Avoid: artifact, resource, plugin, extension.*
- **Five asset types**: `skill`, `rule`, `instruction`, `command`, `persona`. *Avoid "subagent";
  persona is the term.*
- **Manifest** = `harnaas.json`. **Lockfile** = `harnaas.lock.json`. npm-style, deliberately opposite
  to entire.io's usage; do not "correct".
- **Managed** = recorded in the lockfile. **Unmanaged** = not recorded; never touched.
- **Drift** = a managed destination whose content no longer matches what was installed.
- **Managed block** = a marker-delimited region harnaas owns inside a file the team also writes.
- **Shared target** = a destination several harnesses read.
- **Emulated** = installed through a different type's surface because its own is absent.
- **Support tier** = live / gated / legacy / removed; decides whether harnaas writes.
- **Finding** = one problem lint reports, with severity and a runnable fix.

## 2. Manifest (`harnaas.json`)

- Committed, **hand-edited only**. harnaas never writes it.
- **Repository root only.** A manifest in a subdirectory is a validation error naming the root one.
- Strict decoding — unknown fields rejected (committed + human-edited).
- Shape: `version`, `harnesses` (default target list), `sources` (map of key → repo@ref), `assets`
  (array of strings).
- **Type and id are inferred from the path**: the containing directory names the type, the leaf names
  the id. `skills/` → skill, `rules/` → rule, `instructions/` → instruction, `commands/` → command,
  `agents/` → persona. An object form overrides when a source does not follow the convention.
- Asset string forms: `<sourceKey>:<path>` for a declared source, or a `.harnaas/…` relative path for
  a local one.
- Example:
  ```json
  {
    "version": 1,
    "harnesses": ["claude-code"],
    "sources": { "acme": "github:acme/assets@v1.2.0" },
    "assets": [
      "acme:skills/review",
      "acme:commands/deploy",
      ".harnaas/rules/house-style.md",
      ".harnaas/instructions/tone.md"
    ]
  }
  ```
- Version 1 defined; a newer version is refused with upgrade guidance; a missing version is an error.

## 3. Sources

- Kinds registry; v1 registers `github` and `local`.
- **GitHub**: resolve ref → immutable commit over the **Git protocol** (`ls-remote`, uses existing
  credential helpers), then fetch the **repository archive** over HTTPS for that commit and extract
  only the declared subtree. One fetch per repo+commit per run.
- **Local**: read from `.harnaas/` through a handle anchored there (kernel-level containment).
- Security: HTTPS only, plaintext and loopback rejected including after redirect; bounded redirects;
  size ceilings that fail rather than truncate; zip-slip rejection; link/device entries rejected;
  credentials redacted from errors and from anything persisted.
- Auth: `HARNAAS_GITHUB_TOKEN` → `GH_TOKEN` → `GITHUB_TOKEN` → unauthenticated. An authorization
  failure is a distinct, actionable error naming the variable.
- Cache: content-addressed under the user cache dir, `HARNAAS_CACHE_DIR` overrides. Entry verified
  before reuse; corrupt entry discarded and refetched, never fatal. Bypassable.
- **`install --offline`** resolves entirely from cache and fails naming what is not cached.
- Digests: per-file plus a whole-source digest over sorted relative paths + content. File modes
  normalized. A rename changes the digest.

## 4. Targets

- **Shared-first.** `.agents/skills/<id>/SKILL.md` is read by 17 of 23 harnesses; the `AGENTS.md`
  block by 21. Write there first; fall back to a harness's own directory only where the harness does
  not read the shared one.
- **Two tiers of support**: shared targets serve `skill` and `instruction` with no per-harness
  adapter; a **named adapter** adds that harness's own surfaces (`rule`, `command`, `persona`).
  **v1 ships one named adapter: `claude-code`.**
- Claude Code mapping: `rule` → `.claude/rules/<id>.md`; `command` → `.claude/commands/<id>.md`;
  `persona` → `.claude/agents/<id>.md`; plus the `@AGENTS.md` bridge line in `CLAUDE.md`.
- **Scope**: `project` default, `user` opt-in — but an adapter may offer user scope **only where its
  per-user location is unambiguous**. Declaring user scope on an adapter that does not offer it is a
  validation error, never a silent fallback. `instruction` is **project scope only**.
- **Support tiers gate writes**: live → write; **removed → refuse** with an error naming the
  replacement (writing there is a guaranteed silent no-op); gated/preview → write plus a setup note;
  legacy → write plus a deprecation note.
- Destination containment through a handle anchored at the scope root.
- Adapters self-register; registry lookup is deterministic; duplicate registration fails loudly.
- **Adapter import boundary enforced by a hand-written AST test with an allowlist**, not depguard.
  The same test asserts every adapter package self-registers.

## 5. Instruction mechanism

- Marker-delimited **managed block in `AGENTS.md`**, plus harnaas ensuring a single `@AGENTS.md` line
  exists in `CLAUDE.md` (appended at the end; `CLAUDE.md` created containing only that line if
  absent; the line removed, and the file deleted only if it contains nothing else, when no
  instruction assets remain).
- Block content: instruction assets **inlined verbatim**, sorted by asset id, each preceded by an
  HTML comment naming the asset and its source. HTML comments are stripped by Claude Code before the
  model sees them, so provenance costs zero context.
- Everything outside the markers preserved byte-for-byte. Block removed entirely when the last
  instruction asset goes.
- `rule` assets are **never** referenced from this block — they are separate gitignored files.

## 6. Install

- Phases: resolve → plan → apply → record. No harness write before the plan is complete.
- Outcomes per asset × target: `created`, `updated`, `unchanged`, `emulated`, `conflict-unmanaged`,
  `conflict-drift`, `unsupported`. Each blocked outcome carries a runnable remedy.
- **Unmanaged paths are never overwritten — `--force` does not override this.** `--force` applies
  only to drifted managed destinations.
- **Converges**: an asset removed from the manifest has its files deleted — but only destinations
  recorded in the lockfile whose content still matches. A modified orphan is kept and reported.
- **Full uninstall = empty the `assets` array and run install.** Documented, no separate command.
- Atomic: stage outside the destination, land by rename; directories replaced as a unit; staging
  cleaned up on success and failure.
- Exclusive lock around the lockfile read-modify-write, bounded wait, clear contention message.
- Deterministic order by asset id — reordering the manifest changes neither report nor lockfile.
- Partial failure: attempt every asset, report every failure, exit non-zero, record only what landed.
- `--dry-run` computes the same outcomes and writes nothing.
- `--json` emits the report as a single document; advisory text goes to stderr.

## 7. Rendering (install may generate, not only copy)

- Two independent digests per installation: **source digest** (changed → an update is available) and
  **installed digest** (changed → someone edited it). Copying verbatim is the default renderer, not
  an invariant.
- v1 implements two renderers: **identity** (copy bytes unchanged) and **as-skill** (a `command`
  becomes a `SKILL.md` with model invocation disabled, on harnesses with no command surface).
- The adapter interface **declares** a per-type render hook so future adapters need no redesign;
  to-TOML, to-YAML, to-TypeScript and shared-document renderers are specified as capabilities and
  **not implemented** in v1.
- `rule` → `instruction` emulation: allowed **only for a rule with no path scoping** (semantics
  unchanged). A rule declaring `paths:` is reported `unsupported` on a harness with no rules
  directory, rather than silently becoming always-on.
- Frontmatter is otherwise **passed through untouched** — harnaas never rewrites `paths:` or any
  other key.

## 8. Install-time validation

- **Fail** on limits the harness provably enforces: 4 MiB per memory file, 1 MB per `SKILL.md`,
  import depth 5. Installing past these produces a file that is silently skipped.
- **Warn** on the ~40,000-char soft threshold for assembled always-on content.
- **Fail on a skill whose `SKILL.md` frontmatter `name` does not match its inferred id** — Augment,
  Kilo and Cline drop mismatched skills silently. This is a read-only check; content is still copied
  byte-for-byte.
- Shape checks: `skill` must be a directory containing `SKILL.md`; other types a single file.

## 9. Lockfile (`harnaas.lock.json`)

- Committed. Machine-written. **Lenient decoding** (unknown fields ignored — a newer binary must not
  brick an older one); an uninterpretable version is reported, malformed JSON never destroys files.
- Records per asset: id, type, normalized source, requested ref, resolved commit, source digest,
  install time. Per installation: harness, scope, destination, per-file digests, installed digest.
- **Destinations stored relative to the scope root** plus the scope name — never absolute.
- Credentials redacted from any recorded URL.
- Deterministic serialization: identical state → byte-identical file.
- Atomic write under the install lock.
- **Absent lockfile = nothing is managed**, so every pre-existing destination is unmanaged and
  protected. Not an error.

## 10. Version control

- **Installed files are gitignored.** harnaas maintains a **managed block in `.gitignore`** listing
  exactly the paths it installed — regenerated on install, pruned on convergence.
- Coarse directory ignores are explicitly rejected: they would untrack a hand-written skill sitting
  beside an installed one.
- Committed: `harnaas.json`, `harnaas.lock.json`, `AGENTS.md` (with its block), `CLAUDE.md` (with the
  bridge line), `.gitignore` (with its block), and everything under `.harnaas/`.

## 11. Lint

- **Read-only, always.** Never installs, repairs or rewrites. Writing to the user cache is permitted.
  `harnaas install --force` is the single repair path; every finding names it or another command.
- Local checks: manifest invalid (one finding, suppresses dependents — no cascade); declared but not
  installed; stale lockfile entry; content drift (per file); missing file; absent destination
  (collapsed to one finding); extraneous file under a managed destination; unmanaged conflict;
  managed-block drift in `AGENTS.md` or `.gitignore`; missing `@AGENTS.md` bridge line.
- **"Nothing installed at all" collapses to one finding**, not one per asset.
- Update detection: moved mutable ref; vanished ref (distinct from an update); superseded tag
  (highest newer stable tag only, non-version tags ignored, no pre-release over a stable install);
  commit-pinned assets never checked; local source changed; local source deleted (distinct).
- **Severity: an available update is an ERROR. Tracking a mutable ref is an ERROR** ("not
  reproducible — pin it"). The only passing state is pinned and current. Findings print the exact
  before/after edit and the command to follow it with.
- Exit: `0` no errors, `2` any error. `--strict` promotes warnings. A lint *failure* exits `1`.
- `--offline` runs every local check plus local-source change detection, skips the network, and the
  report states what was skipped so a clean result is never mistaken for a complete one.
- **`--frozen`** verifies the lockfile still satisfies the manifest with no files present and no
  network — the fast PR gate on a fresh checkout.
- Graceful degradation: an unreachable host marks assets unchecked, is reported once per host, never
  fails the run, and the summary states how many went unchecked.
- Deterministic finding order; `--json` emits one document, valid even when empty.

## 12. CLI foundation (largely unchanged from the current specs)

- Root command with cobra error/usage printing silenced; **zero persistent flags**; `--json`
  registered locally per command.
- Entrypoint owns error rendering and exit codes. Exit `0` success, `1` runtime failure, `2` lint
  findings, `128+signum` for signals — re-raised, not `os.Exit`.
- Two-stage signal handling with a force-quit escape hatch.
- Project root carried in `context.Context`; `os.Getwd` banned by `forbidigo`.
- Structured logging to a file; **logs must not contain user content**; user output via
  `cmd.OutOrStdout()`, never cobra's `Print*`.
- Every workflow completable non-interactively; accessible prompts; base16-only palette with body
  text unstyled.

## 13. Init (largely unchanged)

- Writes exactly one file, `harnaas.json`. Never edits `.gitignore` (install does that), never
  creates harness directories, never creates `.harnaas/`.
- Detects present harnesses to pre-fill; falls back to the default harness and says so.
- `--force` to replace an existing manifest; refusal names the flag.
- Accessible interactive selection with a complete flag-driven equivalent; auto-selects the
  non-interactive path with no terminal; writes nothing if cancelled.
- Atomic write.

## 14. ADRs recorded at `docs/adr/`

content.text:
The grilling session is complete and the revision is running. Summary of where things stand:

**Written and committed to the repo:**

- `CONTEXT.md` — the glossary, built incrementally as terms resolved. Sixteen terms with opinionated `_Avoid_` lists, including the one that will otherwise get "fixed" later: entire.io uses *manifest* for what we call the lockfile.
- `docs/adr/0001`–`0004` — ownership in the lockfile; shared `.agents/` before per-harness; instruction content in an AGENTS.md block; updates as lint errors. Each records the rejected alternative, since in all four cases the obvious design is not what we chose.

**In flight:** a 13-agent workflow rewriting the nine delta specs and three sets of proposal/design/tasks against a single authoritative ledger, ending with an audit pass that runs `openspec validate --changes --strict` and fixes cross-file drift. One capability is new — `asset-rendering` — because rendering, emulation and install-time validation didn't fit cleanly into any existing spec. That makes `add-harnaas-install` five deltas rather than four; still inside OpenSpec's limit, and it's a capability rather than a fourth change, so it stays within what you approved.

**What the grilling actually changed.** Forty decisions, of which these reversed my original specs outright: installed files are gitignored rather than neutral, the manifest infers type and id from the path instead of declaring them, skills install to a shared directory reaching 17 harnesses rather than per-harness trees, and an available update fails CI rather than warning.

Three of my own claims were wrong along the way, all now corrected in the record: `.claude/rules/` exists and is auto-loaded (I'd invented a workaround for its absence); AGENTS.md is **not** natively read by Claude Code (I asserted it was, citing a string in the binary that turned out to have no loader behind it); and the SKILL.md cap is 1 MB, not 64 KB. The second one had already been baked into an answer you gave, which is why it got flagged mid-round rather than quietly patched.

The load-bearing insight was one you pushed on twice — first asking for `openspec init`'s breadth, then questioning whether `id` and `type` were needed at all. Both pointed at the same thing: the ecosystem has already converged, on `.agents/skills/`, on `AGENTS.md`, and on directory names that encode the type. The design got smaller and reached further as a result.

I'll report the audit output when the workflow lands.

content.text:
Done. The specs now match the design we grilled out.

## Final state

```
CONTEXT.md                    18 terms, opinionated, with _Avoid_ lists
docs/adr/0001–0004            the four load-bearing decisions
openspec/changes/
├── add-harnaas-foundation    3 capabilities   31 requirements
├── add-harnaas-install       5 capabilities   63 requirements
└── add-harnaas-lint          2 capabilities   24 requirements
```

**118 requirements, 337 scenarios, 10 delta specs.** `openspec validate --changes --strict` passes 3/3, zero duplicate requirement headings across all ten specs.

## What I verified myself rather than taking on trust

The audit agent reported clean; I re-ran validation and grepped independently for the three failure modes most likely to have survived, since twelve agents wrote these files in parallel:

- **No file describes referencing rule files from a memory file.** Three hits, all negative statements — `harness-targets` now says rules "MUST NOT be referenced from `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md` or any other file."
- **No file claims Claude Code reads AGENTS.md natively.** Zero hits. That's the error I made twice; it's gone from the record.
- **No file reports an available update as a warning.** One hit, in `add-harnaas-lint/design.md`, explaining why harnaas departs from that convention.

## The two items the audit escalated

**Consolidated:** `Instruction Project Scope Only` was specified in both `harnaas-manifest` and `harness-targets`. I moved it to manifest validation and deleted the adapter-layer copy — it's a property of the *type*, so no adapter could ever vary it, and stating it in the adapter layer implies a variability that doesn't exist. Install task 5.7 now says the adapter relies on that check rather than reimplementing it.

**Left alone:** `asset-rendering`'s *Two Independent Digests* and `install-lockfile`'s *Two Independent Digests Per Installation* overlap in wording but not in subject — one specifies how the digests are computed and what each answers, the other what gets persisted. Collapsing either leaves a real gap. The audit's reasoning was right.

## Where the design landed versus where it started

The grilling changed the substance, not just the wording. Four decisions in the original specs are now inverted: installed files are gitignored rather than neutral; the manifest infers type and id from the path rather than declaring them; skills install to a shared directory reaching 17 harnesses rather than one tree per harness; and an available update fails CI rather than warning. A fifth mechanism — the `CLAUDE.md` rule-reference block — was deleted entirely, because it described something that doesn't exist.

The specs are ready for `/opsx:apply`. No code has been written.
